quarterly_data.quarter: Arteris press release: Arteris Wins Funding to Expand Hardware Design Supply Chain (10-06-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Arteris announced the expansion of its third-party IP (3PIP) security assurance program in collaboration with BAE Systems and SiFive; the program received an additional $3.3 million in funding through the Trusted and Assured Microelectronics (T&AM) program within the Office of the Under Secretary of War for Research and Engineering (OUSW(R&E)). The work aims to establish a repeatable, evidence-based methodology to evaluate and verify the secure implementation, integration and usage of commercially sourced third-party IP in SoCs for mission-critical aerospace and defense systems, using Arteris's Common Weakness Enumeration (CWE)-based microelectronics evidence framework. CEO K. Charles Janac: third-party IP security assurance has become a critical requirement for commercial and government applications, particularly aerospace and defense, data center infrastructure, automotive and intelligent edge devices including drones and robotics.
quarterly_data.counterparty: Trusted and Assured Microelectronics (T&AM) program, OUSW(R&E)
